studies.TITLE: Trailer-week OW only: full-feature model bake-off and range calibration (Parts B, C)
studies.HYPOTHESIS: B: some model family beats CatBoost on the full trailer-week feature set (YT+Wiki+Trends+attrs). C: Mondrian/CQR/normalized conformal for the OW range, and correlated chained intervals for TOTAL4, reach calibrated 80% coverage overall and under/over 60M. Trailer-week data only; V7 is no input or arm.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Quarter-clustered bootstrap (B=20000). B: B1..B10 - B0 mean abs log error (Holm over 10). C: 80% coverage Wilson CI per arm overall and by actual size bucket. Also MdALE, log R2, Winkler, mean/median APE separately, width; subgroups under/over 60M.
studies.DECISION_RULE: B: a method beats CatBoost only if its Holm CI is below 0; recommend the simplest not significantly worse than the best. C: an arm passes if its coverage CI includes 0.80 overall and in each actual-size bucket; narrowest passing arm by Winkler. Frame FRAME_S_1101_0FDC8C TL, cutoff first comment+7d, scored only before D-21, training opens before the quarter's earliest cutoff, Trends from TL_TRENDS_PULL_V2. V7 at most a labelled backtest reference row, in no fit or decision. Attributes as read in 2026 and the outcome-selected universe are stated limits.

studies.TITLE: Chained backtest: trailer-week OW forecast into holdover W2-W4 and 4-weekend total
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Feeding the S-1101-042e4a trailer-week OW forecast into the S-1031-9c3c20 holdover model (as-of features) gives W2-W4 and 4-weekend-total forecasts whose 80% ranges are calibrated on past releases; the gap to the actual-OW ceiling measures the OW leg's cost.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Median abs log error per target (W2,W3,W4,TOTAL4) and 80% coverage with Wilson CI; paired film bootstrap of abs log error vs ceiling (actual OW) and vs V7 (backtest d-21/d-3) on overlap, Holm over 8; subgroups under/over 60M
studies.DECISION_RULE: Descriptive, no promotion. Show-supported only if TOTAL4 80% coverage CI includes 0.80. Same 139 test films and quarters as S-1101-042e4a; holdover trained only on films whose W_k was observable before the quarter's earliest trailer-week cutoff; as-of holdover features only.

studies.TITLE: Same-day data lag: train on windows ending the day before scoring
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Training V7 on demand windows that end one day earlier (matching what live scoring sees) changes out-of-sample aLoss r=2 versus V7 trained on full-day windows, when both are evaluated on lagged (live-like) holdout inputs.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: aLoss r=2, latest horizon per film, on lagged inputs; secondary: per-horizon aLoss, mean MAPE, median APE, range coverage, under/over 60M
studies.DECISION_RULE: Recommend A2 if the paired film bootstrap 95% CI upper bound of (A2 minus A1) aLoss is below 0 at latest horizon, with no horizon or size subgroup worse by more than its CI half-width (Holm). CI spanning 0 = tie, keep V7.
studies.RESULT: A2 (retrain on lagged windows) vs A1 (V7 on lagged inputs, live today), latest horizon, 135 films: aLoss +0.013 [95% CI +0.003, +0.023], worse (Holm p 0.008); under 60M +0.016 [+0.005, +0.026] (112 films); over 60M tie (23). Rule needs upper bound < 0: keep V7. Descriptive live penalty A1 vs A0: aLoss -0.003 [-0.015, +0.009] tie; range misses +3.0 pts [+0.7, +5.9] worse. Deviations: d-21 unlagged (no d-22 rows); comment counts unlagged. Same-day baseline 135 films MAPE 0.369 aLoss 0.504 did not reproduce V7 registration (0.390/0.524); recheck blocked by expired login.

studies.TITLE: Trailer-week feature interactions (V7-style) for the first-comment-week OW model
studies.HYPOTHESIS: At first comment + 7 days, adding V7-style interactions (sentiment x volume, intent x volume, volume x IP, volume x action/horror, star x volume, star x IP) to the same features lowers point error, more for ridge than CatBoost.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: mean |log error| difference, quarter-clustered bootstrap with per-draw relabelling, for yti-ytc and fulli-full under CatBoost and ridge (4 contrasts, Holm). Secondary: median and mean APE separately, 80% conformal width, coverage with Wilson CI, Winkler, ablation volume->+sentiment->+intent, under/over 60M.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Single horizon TL (first comment + 7 days; horizons field is a placeholder). Frame FRAME_S_1101_0FDC8C h=TL, rolling quarters 2023Q1-2026Q3, train opens before earliest test cutoff, 80% split conformal on 5-fold OOF. Interactions help only if Holm p<0.05, CI below 0, and coverage CI includes 0.80. Star power point-in-time from earlier films before cutoff, missing if none. Otherwise tie.
studies.RESULT: TL only (first comment+7d; '21' is a CLI artifact). 139 test films, 10 quarters (2024Q2-2026Q3). V7-style interactions add nothing: mean |log err| diff yti-ytc CB +0.003 [-0.015,0.025], ridge -0.002 [-0.013,0.010]; fulli-full CB +0.008 [-0.007,0.024], ridge 0.000 [-0.011,0.010]; Holm p=1.0 all. Median miss: CB yt 46%, ytc 45%, yti 42%, full 38%, fulli 38%; ridge yt 46%, yti 53%, full 37%, fulli 36%. Coverage 71-78% (all CIs incl 0.80 except ridge ytc/CB fulli borderline). Ablation (uncorrected): ridge +sentiment -0.034 [-0.066,-0.004]; CB not sig; intent not sig. Ten clusters: coarse, a tie, not proof of no effect. Limits: cast billing read in 2026 (CREATED_AT 2026-02-03..10-28, 17 days), no pre-release snapshot; train films selected release<earliest cutoff without +3d lag; star missing 107/251 frame, 34/139 test. Gruney approved run with conditions (reply only, no ledger path).

studies.TITLE: V7 comment leak, redo: does an as-of retrain beat V7 as deployed (trained leaky, scored as-of)?
studies.HYPOTHESIS: A V7-recipe model trained and scored on strict as-of comment features beats V7 as deployed (trained on leaky features, scored on as-of features) on the backtest.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: paired film bootstrap of aLoss r=2 (HDR50 mean, latest horizon per film), asof_asof vs leaky_asof; per horizon and latest; Holm across the 3 comparisons vs leaky_asof (asof_asof, datefix_asof, leaky_leaky). Secondary: mean MAPE and median APE separately, under/over 60M, PRED_OW_POINT. Descriptive: drift of strict as-of vs leaky features, release-date mismatch counts.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Material = Holm CI excludes 0 and |mean aLoss change| >= 0.01 at latest. Features: strict cut date < PRODUCTION.RELEASE_DATES.release_date + DAYS_OUT; the 5 comment-mix features recomputed; YT_COMMENTS and NET_INTENT_PCT from THEATRICAL_STAGING.OW_PREDICTION_FEATURES_ASOF_V; LOG_YT, LOG_YT_PER_TRAILER and all interactions recomputed by the recipe. datefix = comments through PRODUCTION.RELEASE_DATES release day (no horizon cut). V7 recipe (8 temporal blocks, single-thread CatBoost); a cross-holdout trains each block on one feature set and scores the same rows on another. Supersedes S-1101-123765 per Gruney's review R-1102-ddefa5.
studies.RESULT: Strict as-of (date < RELEASE_DATES + DAYS_OUT), YT_COMMENTS and NET_INTENT_PCT from OW_PREDICTION_FEATURES_ASOF_V (0 missing rows), interactions recomputed. 135 films, latest horizon, HDR50 mean, Holm over 3 vs V7 as deployed. V7 as deployed (trained leaky, scored as-of) aLoss 0.523, MAPE 38.0%, median APE 27.4%; its own leaky backtest 0.520 (diff -0.003 [-0.029,+0.019]): the leak does not measurably flatter or hurt deployed V7. As-of retrain (asof_asof) vs deployed: +0.002 [-0.020,+0.023], Holm p 1.0; median APE worse (27.4% to 30.7%). Release-date repair only (datefix_asof: comment-mix features through the PRODUCTION.RELEASE_DATES release day, scored as-of) vs deployed: -0.010 [-0.022,+0.002], Holm p 0.32 at latest; on PRED_OW_POINT -0.017 [-0.029,-0.004] at d-7 (Holm p 0.018), not at other horizons; gain under 60M (-0.015), none over 60M (+0.017, n=23). Most of S-1101-123765's fix5 gain came from the release-date repair, not the horizon cut. Strict drift vs leaky: 5 mix features r 0.90-0.97, LOG_YT median abs 0.060 (r 0.94), NET_INTENT_PCT 0.10 (r 0.97). Release-date defect: 61 of 336 view films have a different release date in YOUTUBE_COMMENTS_SCORED (47 by >30 days, max 1,485; 31 with multiple dates). Recommendation: no retrain for the comment-horizon leak; an as-of retrain does not beat V7 as deployed. The comments table's release-date defect is the more promising fix (data, Lomis), still within noise at the latest horizon; include both in the next scheduled retrain. Evidence is weak either way, so the leak is not shown immaterial.

studies.TITLE: Trailer week = first-comment week (Mike's decision): YouTube, Wikipedia, Google Trends, attributes vs OW range
studies.HYPOTHESIS: At first comment + 7 days (trailer launch = first comment date, decided by Mike 2026-11-01: 'Just use first day of comments it's fine'), adding Google Trends (Lomis's as-of pull), Wikipedia and attributes to YouTube-only narrows the 80% OW range at similar coverage.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: fold-level log width of 80% conformal range vs yt, quarter-clustered bootstrap with per-draw relabelling, Holm across arms vs yt. Secondary (descriptive): interval (Winkler) score, quarter-clustered point error, coverage (CI incl 0.80), OW mean and median APE, source counts, Trends windows excluded for running past the cutoff.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Cutoff = first comment + 7 days, features strictly before it; scored only if before D-21. Training films must open before the quarter's earliest test cutoff. CatBoost, 80% split-conformal on 5-fold OOF. Trends arms run only after Lomis's pull lands, windows ending by the cutoff (ML_RESEARCH.TL_TRENDS_WINDOWS). Narrows only if Holm CI below 0 at coverage CI including 0.80. Attributes as read in 2026, not as-of; Creed III and Equalizer 3 Wikipedia from corrected production rows if applied, else missing.
studies.RESULT: First-comment week, 139 test films in 10 rolling quarters; 107 of them have Trends data. Lomis's 214-film fallback pull, day -7..+6 relative to first comment, scaled to the Movie Showtimes anchor. 80% range width / coverage / median miss: YouTube 5.0x/76%/45%; YT+Wiki+attr 3.8x/74%/43%; Trends alone 5.1x/73%/45%; YT+Trends 3.9x/74%/37%; YT+Trends+attr 3.5x/67%/35%; YT+Trends+Wiki+attr 3.3x/70%/34%. Trends over YT+Wiki+attr: log width -0.135 [-0.171,-0.099], point error -0.048 [-0.081,-0.016] (quarter-clustered). Winkler -0.13 [-0.41,0.16] vs YT, not significant. The Trends arms under-cover 80% (yt_gt_attr 67%, p<0.001; full arm 70%, p=0.004), so part of the narrowing is miscalibration. The point-error gain is promising but not established after Holm (p=0.095). 15-day window, not the 90 days pre-registered.

studies.TITLE: Size the V7 comment-feature hindsight leak (DATE<=RELEASE_DATE) and whether a retrain is worth it
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Rebuilding V7's five comment-mix features (PCT_PASS, PCT_NEG, PCT_THEA, PCT_POS, AVG_SENT) as of each training row's horizon changes V7's backtest accuracy materially.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: paired film bootstrap of aLoss r=2 (V7 output policy, latest horizon per film, same films as base), per horizon d-21/14/7/3 and latest, Holm across arms. Secondary: mean MAPE and median APE separately; under/over 60M. Descriptive: share of comments in [D-21, D-0] per film (median/p10/p90); per-feature median abs change and correlation all-comments vs as-of; serving-query cutoff check.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Material = Holm-adjusted 95% CI excludes 0 AND |mean aLoss change| >= 0.01 at latest horizon. Arms: base (TRAIN_SQL as-is), fix5 (5 features as of release - |DAYS_OUT|), fix5_yt (fix5 plus YT_COMMENTS, LOG_YT, LOG_YT_PER_TRAILER as of horizon). V7 recipe via research_kit.recipe.holdout, single-thread CatBoost, same-day baseline rerun. Research schema only.
studies.RESULT: Leak is small and the retrain gain is not material by the pre-set rule. (1) Volume: V7 universe 270 films; comments dated in the last 21 days before release are a median 6.8% of each film's comments (p10 0.9%, p90 26.1%; pooled 6.6%); last 3 days 1.4%. (2) Drift, as-of vs all-comments at the row's own horizon: PCT_PASS median abs change 0.057 pts (r 0.968), PCT_NEG 0.20 (0.950), PCT_THEA 0.084 (0.931), PCT_POS 0.18 (0.899), AVG_SENT 0.0016 (0.970); LOG_YT 0.034 (0.981). Largest at d-21 (PCT_PASS 0.091) and shrinking to d-3 (0.031). (3) V7 recipe, same-day rerun (base 135 films, MAPE 0.389, aLoss 0.520; registered V7 is 134 films 0.390/0.524, one film added since): fix5 aLoss -0.016 [-0.032,-0.001] at latest horizon (nominal p 0.031, Holm p 0.28), mean MAPE 38.9% to 37.0% but median APE 24.3% to 26.7%; per horizon -0.009 to -0.016, none Holm-significant; gain under 60M (-0.020), none over 60M (+0.003, n=23). fix5_yt -0.008 [-0.025,+0.007] n.s. Same pattern on PRED_OW_POINT. (4) Serving: scoring.py uses the same DATE<=RELEASE_DATE filter, but scores before release so it can only see comments up to the scoring day; it is effectively as-of. The defect is a train/serve mismatch (training rows see up to 21 extra days of comments), not leakage into live predictions. Recommendation: no standalone retrain; make the comment features as-of in the next scheduled retrain for correctness (direction of the effect is favorable, magnitude within noise).

studies.TITLE: Trailer upload week (studio upload date): YouTube, Wikipedia, Trends, attributes vs OW range
studies.HYPOTHESIS: With trailer launch = the studio channel's YouTube upload date (cutoff upload+7d), adding Wikipedia, Google Trends (Lomis's as-of pull, window ending by the cutoff) and attributes to YouTube-only narrows the 80% OW range at similar coverage. Also re-checks S-1101-042e4a's arms on upload-date cutoffs.

Same table reported on the upload-dated films only.

Cutoff = upload+7d, scored only if before D-21. Training films must open before the quarter's earliest test cutoff. CatBoost, 80% split-conformal on 5-fold OOF. studies.RESULT: Not run. Superseded by Mike's decision (2026-11-01, Slack, via Snowy on card task-29a4ec37): 'Just use first day of comments it's fine'. Trailer launch = each film's first comment date; no studio upload dates. Re-registered with first-comment cutoffs.

studies.TITLE: Addendum to S-1101-042e4a: Google Trends at first-comment week
studies.HYPOTHESIS: With Lomis's historical as-of Google Trends pull for each film's first-comment week, adding Trends features (level, spike, growth; within-window pre-cutoff ratios and SCALED_INTEREST only) narrows the 80% OW range at similar coverage vs YouTube only, and adds to YouTube+Wikipedia+attributes.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: fold-level log width of 80% conformal range, quarter-clustered bootstrap vs arm yt, Holm across 4 new arms (gt, yt_gt, yt_gt_attr, yt_gt_tw_attr); increment of yt_gt_tw_attr over yt_tw_attr reported. Secondary: quarter-clustered point error and coverage (descriptive; CI incl 0.80 = calibrated), OW mean and median APE, Trends coverage counts.

Same frame, splits and gap rule as corrected S-1101-042e4a (train only on films opened before the quarter's earliest test cutoff), CatBoost, 80% split-conformal on 5-fold OOF. Trends must be pulled with the window ending at or before each film's cutoff; any window extending past the cutoff is excluded and counted. Runs only after Lomis's pull lands.
studies.RESULT: Not run; no Trends pulled. Superseded before any data: Gruney's rule (via Snowy, 2026-11-01) defines trailer launch as the studio's YouTube channel upload date, not the first comment. Re-registered with upload-date cutoffs.

studies.TITLE: Trailer-launch week only: do Wikipedia (+Trends) and attributes narrow the YouTube OW range?
studies.HYPOTHESIS: At trailer launch + 7 days (launch = first YouTube comment date), adding as-of Wikipedia daily pageviews (level, spike, growth; Trends where present) and known-at-the-time attributes to the YouTube-only model narrows the 80% OW range at equal coverage.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: per-film log width of 80% conformal range, paired film bootstrap vs arm yt, Holm across 5 arm comparisons at one horizon (TL). Win needs 80% coverage CI incl 0.80. Also Winkler, mean abs log error, OW mean and median APE (separately), coverage for no-comment films, source counts.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Narrows only if Holm CI on log width vs yt is below 0 with calibrated coverage. Same universe and rolling quarterly splits as S-1031-5d20a5 (training films opened before quarter start - 21d); CatBoost for every arm; 80% split-conformal on 5-fold OOF. Trends: in-house only, pre-cutoff within-window features; expected near-absent at TL (reported, not imputed). Scope set by Mike 2026-10-31.
studies.RESULT: TL = first YouTube comment + 7 days; 180 test films (rolling quarterly 2023Q3-2026Q3), 251 films have a TL cutoff before D-21. Sources at TL: YouTube 251, Wikipedia >=7 days 234 (spike computable 214), Google Trends 2 (untestable in-house). 80% conformal ranges: YouTube only 4.9x wide, coverage 72% [65,78] (under-covers). YouTube+Wikipedia+attributes 3.8x, coverage 77% [70,82]: log width -0.209 [-0.226,-0.191], Holm p 0.001; point error -0.052 [-0.093,-0.013]; OW mean APE 56% vs 63%, median 42% vs 45%; Winkler -0.203 [-0.438,+0.049] (n.s.). YouTube+attributes 4.1x, 76% [69,81]: -0.152. YouTube+Wikipedia without attributes 4.4x but 72% coverage (CI excludes 0.80), so not a calibrated win. Wikipedia(+Trends) alone 5.1x, wider than YouTube. By the pre-set rule, yt_attr and yt_tw_attr narrow the range at calibrated coverage; most of the gain is from attributes, Wikipedia adds ~0.06 log on top. Caveats: conformal width is constant within a fold, so the per-film width CI understates fold-level uncertainty; every TL film has comments by construction (TL is defined from the first comment), so no no-comment subgroup; universe outcome-selected (OW>=7M); MPAA as-of date unknown; release date is final, not as-scheduled.

studies.TITLE: Addendum to S-1031-5d20a5: Google Trends + Wikipedia around trailer launch, long-range OW range width
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Adding as-of Wikipedia daily pageviews and in-house Google Trends (trailer-drop level, spike, decay, growth) and known-at-the-time attributes to the YouTube-only model narrows the 80% OW range at equal coverage at trailer launch+7, D-90, D-60, D-30, D-21.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: per-film log width of the 80% conformal range, paired film bootstrap vs arm yt, Holm across 6 arms x 5 horizons; a win needs 80% coverage CI to include 0.80. Also Winkler, point mean abs log error, OW mean and median APE, no-comment-film coverage, source counts by horizon.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Narrows only if Holm CI on log width vs yt is below 0 with calibrated coverage. Same universe, rolling quarterly splits and conformal logic as S-1031-5d20a5; one learner (CatBoost) for every arm. Trends used only via pre-cutoff within-window ratios and SCALED_INTEREST; Trends before D-21 untestable in-house.
studies.RESULT: Re-scoped by Mike before any result was produced or viewed (2026-10-31: 'Just for the week of a trailer launch'). The 5-horizon run was stopped mid-way with no table written. Replaced by a trailer-launch-week-only pre-registration. Data facts recorded: in-house Google Trends has >=7 pre-cutoff days for at most 6 of 256 films at any horizon (pulls start ~D-21); Wikipedia daily views pulled as-of from the Wikimedia API for 254 of 256 films.

studies.TITLE: Daily post-opening decay v2: envelope x day-of-week wave, days 1-56, 7 origins
studies.HYPOTHESIS: From the Monday after OW (F0) and after each later weekend (F1-F6), at least one of 10 methods (decay x DOW, generalized gamma, damped oscillation, hierarchical pooling, Holt-Winters, analogs, fPCA clusters, day-level GBM, N-BEATS-style net, ensemble) beats OW x median daily shape (B0) on daily mean abs log error.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: per-film daily mean abs log error over remaining observed days, paired film bootstrap vs B0, Holm across 10 methods x 7 origins = 70. Descriptive (unadjusted): vs seasonal-naive B1, gross-weighted error, weekly and cumulative error, film-grouped conformal 80% coverage by origin x days-ahead, weekday vs weekend, holidays.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Beats B0 at an origin only if Holm CI excludes 0. Recommend the simplest method (pre-set complexity order) within +0.02 log of the best at the upper 95% bound. Label lag: open + 55 + 2 days < quarter start. Missing on-chart days unobserved, not zero; cumulative only for fully observed films. 2-hour compute limit per method, else 'not run'. Plan fixed in daily_decay_v2.md.
studies.RESULT: 492 wide films with daily runs (10 excluded: opening Fri-Sun missing); 273 fully observed through day 56; 472 with no missing on-chart day; opening Fri-Sun daily sum = Mojo weekend within 2% for 491. Primary (per-film daily mean abs log error vs B0 = OW x median daily shape; Holm over 10 methods x 7 origins; n films 354 at F0 to 232 at F6): day-level GBM is best or tied-best at every origin and is the pre-set pick (simplest within +0.02 of best) at F0-F3, F5, F6; ensemble picked at F4. gbm_day vs B0: F0 -0.146 [-0.183,-0.108], F1 -0.211 [-0.250,-0.170], F2 -0.177, F3 -0.130, F4 -0.076, F5 -0.064, F6 -0.086 (all Holm p<=0.018). Classic decay curves also beat B0 early (F0: BOXMOD gen-gamma -0.082, Weibull decay x DOW -0.071, hierarchical -0.054, analogs -0.065, N-BEATS-style net -0.080), with smaller gains later. Damped oscillation and per-film Holt-Winters are worse than B0 (HW +0.126 to +0.140 at F2-F3); fPCA clusters near B0. Seasonal naive B1 is worse than B0 at F1+. Cumulative total error (190 fully observed films): gbm_day 0.204 at F0 vs B0 0.230, 0.091 vs 0.106 at F1. Conformal 80% daily coverage 77-81% overall but under-covers Fri-Sun (67-75%) and holidays (50-72%): needs a weekend/holiday stratum. Event-film exclusion leaves results unchanged. BOXMOD reached its 2-hour budget only in its final quarter (7,300 s at F0, 7,216 s at F1) and scored all films. Holt-Winters equals B0 at F0/F1 by construction. Next: shadow-test gbm_day on films opening from now.

studies.TITLE: Addendum to S-1031-9c3c20: neural nets and NGBoost on holdover W2-W4
studies.HYPOTHESIS: On the 9c3c20 frame (Mojo, approved by Mike 2026-10-31 22:57 UTC), MLPs (16, 64x32, 128x64; standardized X and y, early stopping) and NGBoost (Normal) beat the constant drop for log(Wk/W1), settings A (k=2,3,4) and B (k=3,4), and are not shown worse than CatBoost.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Mean abs log error per target vs constant, paired film bootstrap, Holm across the addendum's own 4 methods x 5 targets = 20 comparisons (full universe primary; matched-film cut reported). Vs CatBoost from 9c3c20: paired CI, nominal (unadjusted), 'not shown worse' if CI includes 0. Coverage of 80% conformal and NGBoost native intervals with binomial CI; native intervals descriptive only.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Beats constant only if Holm CI excludes 0. No equivalence claims. Same frame, splits, label-lag rule and conformal logic as 9c3c20; no tuning on test.
studies.RESULT: Mojo frame of S-1031-9c3c20 (approved by Mike 2026-10-31 22:57 UTC). Holm over 4 methods x 5 targets. Full universe (n=333-358): A:W2 no method beats constant (best mlp128x64 -0.009 [-0.022,+0.004]). A:W3 mlp64x32 -0.075, mlp128x64 -0.079, ngboost -0.106 [-0.154,-0.059] beat constant; A:W4 all four (ngboost -0.167 [-0.227,-0.109]); B:W3/W4 all four (ngboost -0.282 / -0.358). Matched films (n=263-267): only B:W3/W4 survive Holm; A:W2-W4 none (ngboost A:W4 -0.062, Holm p 0.096). Vs CatBoost, nominal/unadjusted: MLPs worse at W3/W4 in both cuts (e.g. full B:W4 mlp64x32 +0.064 [+0.030,+0.097]), not shown worse at W2; NGBoost not shown worse on full at A:W3/A:W4/B:W3/B:W4 (CIs include 0), nominally worse at A:W2 (+0.011 [+0.001,+0.020]) and on matched at most targets (+0.010 to +0.024, lower bounds 0.000-0.005). NGBoost native Normal intervals fail calibration (coverage 31-48% at 1.3-2.2x); with conformal intervals 76-83%. Conclusion unchanged: trees (CatBoost/RF) remain the holdover choice; neural nets do not help; NGBoost is close to CatBoost on points but needs conformal intervals.

studies.TITLE: Daily post-opening box-office decay (envelope x day-of-week wave), days 1-56
studies.HYPOTHESIS: A model of daily gross after opening (decay envelope x day-of-week wave with holiday/school effects, or a curve/analog/sequence alternative) beats 'OW x average daily shape' on daily, weekly and cumulative error, from the Monday after OW and at each weekly re-forecast.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: daily mean abs log error over remaining days, paired film bootstrap vs B0, Holm across method x origin; secondary weekly and cumulative error, APE, 80% coverage with CI, width, n per origin
studies.DECISION_RULE: Beats B0 at an origin only if Holm CI excludes 0; recommend the simplest method not significantly worse than the best. Rolling quarterly origin 2023Q1-2026Q3; training films need a full 56-day run before the quarter. RUN BLOCKED until per-film daily data is cleared (Mojo paused pending Mike).
studies.RESULT: Not run. Superseded by a v2 pre-registration incorporating Gruney's pre-run design review (label-lag date test, missing-day definition, day-1 rule, event-film rule, film-grouped conformal by origin x days-ahead, 70-comparison Holm family, B0 primary + seasonal-naive B1, complexity order with +0.02 non-inferiority margin, compute limit).

studies.TITLE: Addendum to S-1031-5d20a5: neural nets and NGBoost, YouTube-only long-range OW
studies.HYPOTHESIS: With standardized inputs and standardized log target plus early stopping, MLPs (sizes 16, 64x32, 128x64), an MLP on comment stats + 16 PCA embedding components, and NGBoost (Normal) beat climatology at D-60/30/21 and are not worse than CatBoost from S-1031-5d20a5.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Mean abs log error and 80% Winkler, paired film bootstrap vs climatology, Holm across addendum method x horizon; secondary vs CatBoost (same preds file), coverage with CI, width, n per horizon (168/168/184; no cross-horizon comparison)
studies.DECISION_RULE: Beats climatology only if Holm CI excludes 0; 'as good as CatBoost' only if paired CI vs CatBoost includes 0. Same frame (FRAME_S_1031_5D20A5, EMB_S_1031_5D20A5), same rolling quarterly splits, split-conformal 80% from OOF residuals; NGBoost reported both native (Normal q10/q90) and conformal. Holdover (9c3c20) excluded: its data is quarantined pending Mike.
studies.RESULT: YouTube only (holdover excluded: Mojo data quarantined pending Mike). With standardized X and y plus early stopping the MLP failure is gone (64x32 pred SD 0.63-0.74 vs target 0.89, r 0.53-0.66). Point error vs climatology, Holm-significant for every method at D-60/30/21. Best: D-21 emb_mlp 0.523 and mlp128x64 0.524 (climatology 0.740); D-30 emb_mlp 0.529; D-60 ngboost 0.600, mlp128x64 0.610. Vs CatBoost from S-1031-5d20a5 (paired, same films): mlp128x64 and emb_mlp tie at D-21 (+0.021 [-0.017,+0.058]; +0.020 [-0.028,+0.069]) and D-30; mlp16 worse everywhere; ngboost worse at D-30 (+0.039 [+0.010,+0.067]) and D-60 (+0.031 [+0.006,+0.055]), tie at D-21. 80% Winkler Holm-significant only for mlp128x64 and emb_mlp at D-21. NGBoost native Normal intervals collapse: coverage 15-21% at 1.2-1.3x width (Winkler far worse than climatology); with conformal intervals coverage is 73-80%. Conclusion unchanged: neural nets and NGBoost do not beat trees; no standalone build. Earlier note that NGBoost was not installable was wrong: the venv lacked pip; fixed with python -m ensurepip.

studies.TITLE: Bake-off: YouTube-only long-range OW across model families
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Among 15 methods (climatology, ridge, lasso, RF, CatBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost, quantile GBM, distributional GBM, kNN, MLP, embeddings+ridge, embeddings+GBM, velocity-curve GBM, ensemble) on YouTube-comment data only, at least one beats climatology at D-60/30/21 on log-OW error and 80% Winkler score.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Mean abs log error and 80% Winkler, paired film bootstrap vs climatology, Holm across all method x horizon comparisons; secondary aLoss r=2, MdAPE, coverage with CI, width, n, under/over 60M; V7 D-21 backtest reference on overlap
studies.DECISION_RULE: Beats climatology at H only if Holm CI excludes 0; calibrated if 80% coverage CI includes 0.80; claims vs V7 only at D-21 on overlap. Rolling quarterly origin 2023Q1-2026Q3; training films opened before quarter start minus H.
studies.RESULT: YouTube-only, rolling quarterly 2023Q1-2026Q3, Holm across method x horizon. Point error vs climatology: every method except MLP and velocity-curve GBM beats it at D-60/30/21 (e.g. D-60 catboost -0.177 [-0.246,-0.106], D-30 emb_gbm -0.248, D-21 ensemble -0.242). 80% Winkler, Holm-significant: D-60 catboost -0.419, ensemble -0.440, emb_ridge -0.396; D-30 catboost -0.582, ensemble -0.581; D-21 most methods. Embeddings add little over comment stats (D-60 emb_gbm 0.560 vs catboost 0.569). Velocity curves alone are near climatology. Conformal 80% intervals calibrated (cov 75-82%) but 4.4-6.6x wide; native quantile/distributional GBM under-cover (41-55%). MLP failed to fit (uncentred log target; implementation failure, not a verdict). V7 reference at D-21 (staging backtest, n=111 overlap): V7 0.370 vs best YT 0.487-0.494, YT minus V7 +0.12 [+0.04,+0.20]; V7 [low,upside] cov 65% at 2.2x. No-change: no standalone build; long-range value vs climatology only, at 5.6-6.6x range width at D-60.

studies.TITLE: Bake-off: holdover W2-W4 across model families
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Among 14 model families (constant, hierarchical pooling, ridge, lasso, RF, CatBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost, quantile GBM, distributional GBM, Weibull decay curve, kNN analogs, MLP, ensemble), at least one beats the constant-drop baseline for log(Wk/W1), k=2..4, forecast the Monday after OW.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Mean abs log error per k, paired film bootstrap vs constant, Holm across all method x target comparisons; secondary MdAPE, 80% coverage with CI, width, n
studies.DECISION_RULE: Beats baseline at k only if Holm CI excludes 0; recommend the simplest method not significantly worse than the best. Rolling quarterly origin 2023Q1-2026Q3; label-lag rule; no test tuning.
studies.RESULT: Mean abs log error vs constant drop, rolling quarterly 2023Q1-2026Q3, Holm across method x target. Matched in-house films (n=263-267): Monday after OW W2 no method beats constant (best knn -0.008 [-0.022,+0.005]); W3 ensemble -0.048 [-0.077,-0.023] and RF -0.046 sig, catboost not after Holm; W4 catboost -0.087 [-0.130,-0.045], ensemble -0.079, RF -0.078, knn -0.063 sig. After W2 is known: every method except hierarchical beats constant; best W3 ensemble 0.210 vs 0.420, W4 catboost 0.362 vs 0.641. All wide Mojo films (n=333-358): same ranking, larger gains (W3 ensemble -0.124, W4 catboost -0.186); W2 none after Holm. Hierarchical pooling, Weibull curve and MLP do not beat constant; LightGBM and MLP worse at W2. Conformal 80% intervals cover 78-85% (calibrated); native quantile GBM 46-55% and distributional GBM 62-69% under-cover. Recommend: constant drop for W2; tree model (RF or CatBoost; ensemble no better) with split-conformal intervals for W3/W4, and the after-W2 re-forecast. Caveats: Mojo figures as shown today (post-revision); realized opener counts; survivorship (films off chart dropped); event films not flagged.

studies.TITLE: YT-only model on low-comment films (<50 comments)
studies.HYPOTHESIS: For wide films with fewer than 50 YouTube comments before horizon (incl. zero), a YT-only model (log1p count, has-any flag, log trailers, days since first) trained on all wide films beats the naive median of log OW at D-60/D-30/D-21; and is no worse than V7@D-21 where V7 exists.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: mean abs log error on the <50 subset, paired film bootstrap 95% CI (2000 reps); MdAPE and bias secondary
studies.DECISION_RULE: Build-worthy only if CI of (YT - naive) excludes 0 below at a horizon AND CI of (YT - V7) does not exclude 0 above where V7 n>=20; otherwise don't-build stands
studies.RESULT: Low-comment (<50) wide films are almost all zero-comment (D-60 91/92, D-30 62/64, D-21 57/58): a collection gap, not low buzz. YT-only ridge (log count, has-any, log trailers, days-since-first, trained on all wide films) vs naive median, mean abs log error on 2023Q1+ test films: D-60 n=48 +0.012 [-0.074,+0.095]; D-30 n=30 -0.009 [-0.201,+0.169]; D-21 n=25 +0.066 [-0.094,+0.234]. Tie with naive everywhere; error ~1.3-1.5 log for all arms. Vs V7@D-21 where present: D-60 n=10 +0.658 [+0.257,+1.141] (V7 better); D-30 n=3, D-21 n=1 too few. Don't-build stands.

studies.TITLE: Challenge Lomis BOMT: holdover W2 flags and YT-beyond-volume
studies.HYPOTHESIS: H1: an event/fan-release flag plus a holiday-weekend-of-W2 flag cuts W2 (holdover weekend 2) mean abs log error vs naive constant drop on our films. H2: no YouTube comment feature beyond volume adds OOS skill for log OW at D-21 once log trailer count and collection-window length are controlled. H3: data exists in SPARK_PAR_DEMO that Lomis did not use.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: mean abs log error (paired film bootstrap 95% CI, 2000 reps); MdAPE secondary
studies.DECISION_RULE: H1 adopt if CI of (flagged GBM minus naive) on W2 excludes 0 below; H2 rejected only if CI of (controlled+feature minus controlled) excludes 0 below for some feature after Holm
studies.RESULT: H1: event+holiday-W2 flags do not beat naive constant drop on W2 (our films n=176: best arm rich+cal+Wed-theater-change -0.017 [-0.040,+0.005]; rich+cal -0.010 [-0.033,+0.013]); flags help event subgroup (n=12, naive 0.50 -> 0.41) only. H2: controlling log trailers and log days-since-first changes nothing vs volume (+-0.003); no single YT feature beats controlled volume after Holm at D-60/30/21; 8-PC comment embedding is consistently -0.034 to -0.043 (raw p 0.007-0.021, Holm 0.08-0.23) = lead, not finding. H3: GDELT_OW/GDELT_OW_POL null for all 429 films in Lomis sandbox; memo's rich-minus-naive CIs not produced by test1.py; Quorum tracking only 29 films; showtimes baseline market-level only. Lomis BOMT conclusions stand.

studies.TITLE: Holdover multiple: log(total/OW) on OW Monday
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Given actual OW, a model on data knowable by OW Monday predicts log(TOTAL/OW) better than the best simple baseline (constant, genre-median or MPAA-median multiple). Arm wom adds opening-weekend word-of-mouth signals from all in-house sources (YouTube comment volume/sentiment/pass intent on days 0-2, Wikipedia and Google Trends days 0-2 vs pre-release, GDELT days 0-2).
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: mean abs log error of the multiple, paired film bootstrap vs best baseline. Secondary: aLoss r=2, mean MAPE and median APE of implied total (separately), 80% interval coverage, under/over 60M, 5 worst films.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Model beats best baseline if the 95% paired CI excludes 0 AND it wins most rolling quarterly folds; otherwise tie. Universe: OW>=7M, released 2022-01-01..2026-08-31. Split: train before 2025-07-01, test after, plus quarterly rolling origin. RT scores excluded (no proof known by OW Monday).
studies.RESULT: Tie. Main split (train 177 pre-2025-07, test 57): best arm gbm_wom (base + OW-weekend YouTube volume/sentiment/intent, Wikipedia and Trends ratios) mean abs log error 0.266 vs constant multiple 0.298, diff -0.032, 95% CI [-0.070, +0.002]; wins 8/11 quarterly folds. CI includes 0, so the rule fails. aLoss 0.455 vs 0.484; median APE of implied total 22.2% vs 23.1%. Genre/MPAA medians no better than constant. 80% interval coverage 56-60% (under-covers). Post-hoc sensitivity without 2 suspect totals (The Drama total=OW, THE HOUSEMAID round 200M): diff -0.024 [-0.059, +0.006], still a tie. GDELT has no rows in the OW window. Per-weekend (wk2-4) targets need a per-film weekend table.

studies.TITLE: YT-only long-range OW range model
studies.HYPOTHESIS: A model using only YouTube trailer-comment data available before d-H (volume, unique commenters, videos, velocity, recency, intent shares, sentiment, has-comments flag) gives better-calibrated and sharper OW ranges at d-90/60/42 than a climatology baseline (training-set log-OW quantiles).
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Horizons d-90/60/42 plus d-21 reference (not CLI horizons). Primary: 80% interval (Winkler) score on log OW, paired film bootstrap vs climatology, per horizon. Secondary: coverage of 50%/80% ranges, median width ratio, point aLoss r=2, median APE; subgroups under/over 60M.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Shadow-test if at d-90 AND d-60 the paired interval-score diff vs climatology has 95% CI below 0 and 80% coverage is within 70-90%. Otherwise no-change. Films: OW>=7M, release 2022+, temporal expanding-window CV by release date (train on earlier films only), conformal widths from past-only residuals.
studies.RESULT: Rule met for yt_catboost. 80% Winkler score on log OW vs climatology: d-90 -0.410 [-0.638, -0.176] (n=183, cov80 77%); d-60 -0.378 [-0.632, -0.114] (n=187, cov80 74%); d-42 -0.452 [-0.705, -0.173]; d-21 -0.497 [-0.758, -0.230]. Median 80% range high/low ratio about 6x vs 10.6x for climatology. Point aLoss d-90 0.975 vs 1.102; median APE 55% vs 65%. yt_ridge passes d-60 but not d-90. Weak spots: over-60M films cov80 52-58% with no significant Winkler gain (n=29-31); about a third of films have no comments at d-90 and fall back to roughly climatology. Not compared with V7 (no V7 record at d-90/60). Caveats: comments scraped after the fact (deleted comments missing; trailer selection made in hindsight); release dates are final, not as-scheduled at d-H.

studies.TITLE: Holdover model: weekends 2-6 after OW
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Given the actual OW (known the Monday after opening), a model using all data knowable by that Monday (OW, opening theaters, opening day-of-week, genre, MPAA, IP/sequel, studio tier, RT critic score, OW-weekend YouTube/Wikipedia/Trends/GDELT activity and its pre-release ratio, next-weekend wide-opener competition, holidays) predicts weekend-k gross (k=2..6) better than the median-drop baseline.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Weekends k=2..6 (not OW horizons). Primary: aLoss r=2 on log weekend-k gross, paired film bootstrap vs baseline (W_k = OW x training-median ratio for week k), per k, Holm across arms. Secondary: mean MAPE and median APE (separately), 80% range coverage, total-gross multiplier error; subgroups OW under/over 60M.
studies.DECISION_RULE: Recommend shadow if aLoss improves vs baseline with Holm-adjusted 95% CI below 0 at k=2 and k=3 and is not significantly worse at k=4-6. Ties are no-change. Target source: Box Office Mojo weekend charts scraped to ML_RESEARCH; temporal expanding-window CV by release date.
studies.RESULT: Not run. Target needed per-film weekend grosses; the Box Office Mojo scrape was quarantined (~/brown_work/quarantine_do_not_use) and Lomis's card sets total/OW multiple as the target, with weekends 2-4 marked needs-more-data. Replaced by a new pre-registration.

studies.TITLE: YouTube-comments-only long-range OW (D-60/D-30/D-21)
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Comment-only features forecast log OW at D-60/30/21 with calibrated 80% intervals, compared with a V7 backtest on the same films
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: aLoss r=2; coverage 80%; median high/low ratio
studies.DECISION_RULE: Useful if coverage 75-85% and D-21 aLoss not worse than V7 by CI; better only if Holm CI excludes 0 (Holm across D-60, D-30, D-21)
studies.RESULT: Comment-only models carry real long-range signal (best arm gbm+AI_EMBED beats naive median by aLoss -0.26/-0.34/-0.40 at D-60/30/21, CIs exclude 0) with calibrated 80% intervals (coverage 80/81/81% on 134 held-out films), but they lose to V7 at D-21 at every horizon: aLoss +0.41 [+0.29,+0.53] / +0.31 [+0.19,+0.44] / +0.25 [+0.14,+0.36], Holm p<0.001. Intervals ~3x V7's width (median hi/lo 7.5/5.7/6.1 vs 2.2). V7 has no D-60/D-30 features, so the bar was V7 at D-21. Same-day V7 rerun gave 135 films, MAPE 0.385, aLoss 0.518 (registered 134 / 0.390 / 0.524).

studies.TITLE: Holdover multiple (Monday after OW)
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Monday-after-OW model predicts log(TOTAL/OW) better out-of-time than constant, genre and MPAA decay baselines
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: mean abs log error of multiple (paired film bootstrap vs best baseline)
studies.DECISION_RULE: Build only if CI excludes 0 vs best baseline AND majority of rolling folds improve
studies.RESULT: Tie. Monday-after-OW ridge/GBM do not beat constant, genre or MPAA multiple baselines out of time: 58 test films, ridge vs constant mean abs log err -0.004 [-0.031,+0.022], Holm p=1.00; rolling wins 4/8 (ridge), 3/8 (GBM). 2025H2-only robustness (30 films): -0.010 [-0.055,+0.037]. wk2-4 needs more data (no per-film weekend table). 2026 totals look stale (multiple bias +0.22 to +0.30 log for 2026 releases).

studies.TITLE: Interval calibration of the published range (past-only conformal)
studies.HYPOTHESIS: The backtest coverage of the published range is optimistic because its residual bank includes each film's own and later residuals; a past-only bank lowers coverage below 68%, and past-only split conformal on log residuals (pooled C1 or Mondrian by horizon C2) restores latest-per-film coverage to a 95% CI containing 68% without worsening log interval score
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: Primary: range coverage latest-per-film and per horizon (target 68%); secondary: log interval score, width, aLoss r=2 of the point, under/over 60M; paired film bootstrap 10000, Holm across C1,C2 vs P0
studies.DECISION_RULE: Optimism confirmed if P0 miss minus BASE miss CI excludes 0 (latest). Shadow-candidate for the C arm whose latest coverage 95% CI contains 68% while P0's lies below 68%, with iscore vs P0 not worse (CI spans 0 or below) and no horizon/size subgroup iscore worse with CI excluding 0; prefer C1 if both. Else no-change if P0 already ~68%, otherwise inconclusive
studies.RESULT: Optimism confirmed; no calibration arm qualifies. 101 films (temporal blocks 3-8), latest per film. Coverage of published range: BASE (pooled bank, as backtest) 66.3% [57.4,75.2]; P0 (past-only bank, as live) 57.4% [47.5,67.3]; P0 miss minus BASE +0.089 [95% CI +0.040,+0.149], worse at every horizon; aLoss and iscore tie. C1 past-only split conformal 56.4% [46.5,66.3]; C2 Mondrian by horizon 54.5% [44.6,64.4]: neither CI contains 68%, so rule 2 fails. Past-only q16/q84 under-cover => errors grow over time (non-exchangeable). Conformal iscore worse <60M (C1 +0.245 [+0.135,+0.350], n=82) and better >=60M (-0.452 [-0.842,-0.068], n=19): error scale depends on size. Point aLoss unchanged by construction. Same-day V7 recipe: 135 films (registered 134), MAPE 0.393, aLoss 0.524, within tolerance; reproduces() False on film count only. Next: adaptive/recency-weighted conformal, Mondrian by predicted size tier.

studies.TITLE: IP framework v1 relabel (Mike-approved candidate 2026-10-21)
studies.HYPOTHESIS: Relabeling KNOWN_IP_TIER by the written framework (brand-strength 0-3, Mike's spin-off and public-domain rules) and filling missing page-verified predecessors lowers V7-recipe aLoss(r=2) on the temporal holdout versus V7 retrained same-day on current labels.
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: aLoss r=2, paired film bootstrap on the temporal holdout (latest-per-film and d-21/14/7/3), MAPE and median APE secondary; per-IP-tier error before/after
studies.DECISION_RULE: Adopt-candidate only if paired aLoss diff 95% CI excludes 0 in favour of the arm on latest-per-film AND no horizon or size subgroup (<60M/>=60M) worsens with CI excluding 0; Holm across 2 arms. Otherwise tie/reject. Holdout reused, so any win is provisional pending shadow.
studies.RESULT: Tie. Same-day V7 recipe, 135 holdout films, latest per film: aLoss BASE 0.532; A (tiers) 0.517, diff -0.015 [95% CI -0.038, +0.007], Holm p 0.18; B (tiers + 2 verified predecessors) 0.513, diff -0.019 [-0.042, +0.002], Holm p 0.16. No horizon/subgroup better; A worse for >=60M at d-21 (+0.050 [+0.003, +0.099]) and d-14 (+0.054 [+0.009, +0.101]). The model sees IP only via PCTILE_X_IP_HIGH and PCTILE_X_PREDOW, so relabeling moves little. Labels are cleaner (tier-3 OW range 23-360M vs 5.8-360M) but 43 overrides were set with outcomes visible, so the backtest is optimistic. Recommend: adopt labels as data hygiene only after Mike reviews changes and Lomis page-verifies 17 suspect predecessors; no model change.

studies.TITLE: Live vs backtest accuracy gap (graded films)
studies.HYPOTHESIS: The live gap (median APE 52%, coverage 6/16) is explained mainly by input defects fixed in V7 and horizon/size mix plus sampling noise, not by model error beyond the backtest distribution
studies.PRIMARY_METRIC: coverage of published range; median APE; aLoss r=2 (primary); mean MAPE separately; log bias
studies.DECISION_RULE: Input-defect explanation holds if V5_CORR restores coverage to within the binomial 95% CI of the mix-matched backtest coverage; intervals miscalibrated if V7_CORR coverage is below the mix-matched backtest coverage at p<0.05; otherwise inconclusive at n=16, re-check at n>=30
studies.RESULT: Live REC coverage 7/16 (95% CI 20-70%) vs mix-matched backtest 63.5%, p=0.12; median APE 52% at 99th pctile of BT. Pre-registered V5_CORR 11/16 and V7_CORR 14/16 are in-sample (14/16 and 16/16 films in training), so the rule cannot be applied. Unregistered out-of-fold arm on corrected inputs: 6/16 (CI 15-65%), p=0.038 below BT; OOF-REC aLoss -0.06 [-0.28,+0.14] tie. n=16 of 19 graded.

note: Brown's pre-registered studies, challenger models and shadow forecasts (no inputs or evidence files)
